🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Industry Posts Its Fastest Growth in 33 Months</u>

Mexico's industrial output rose 2.4% year-on-year in July — its strongest annual growth in 33 months, per INEGI data reported by El Economista — led by construction up 6.7% and mining up 1.6%. Month-on-month, industry gained 0.5%, with construction (+0.9%) and manufacturing (+0.7%) driving the advance, as the peso holds near 16.9 to the dollar, its best level of the year.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Fuel-Theft Crackdown: 7.9 Million Liters Seized in Guanajuato</u>

The FGR raided a property in Salamanca, Guanajuato and found a five-meter vertical tank holding 35,000 liters of stolen diesel — pushing the total seized in the state to nearly 7.9 million liters, worth over 189 million pesos, across 106 raids this administration. Investigators also hauled off a computer and DVR to trace the distribution network.

🇲🇽📚 <u>OECD Says Mexico's Public-School Model Is Closing the Equity Gap</u>

Mexico's Nueva Escuela Mexicana is drawing international recognition: in PISA, the science gap between advantaged and disadvantaged students is 68 points, well below the 85-point OECD average; 82% of Mexican students say they ask teachers for help (OECD 77%), and only 11% see school as a waste of time versus 24% across the OECD. Sheinbaum called it "a distinct pedagogy, recognized internationally" — not the old teacher-centered classroom.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Chiapas: 9,900 Arrests, 18 Tons of Drugs, Homicides Down 64%</u>

Security chief Omar García Harfuch reported from Tuxtla Gutiérrez that since October 2024 operations in Chiapas have detained over 9,900 people for high-impact crimes, seized 1,545 firearms, 97,400 cartridges and more than 18 tons of drugs, and dismantled three meth labs — while the state's daily homicide average fell 64%. "Wherever there is a generator of violence, there will be an investigation, and there will be no impunity."

🇲🇽🪶 <u>No Government Has Recognized Indigenous Peoples Like the 4T</u>

From Oaxaca's Guelaguetza auditorium, Sheinbaum signed a consultation reaching 16,728 communities of Mexico's 69 indigenous peoples and the Afro-Mexican people on a new General Law of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Rights — and moved to write their infrastructure fund into the Constitution. She called them "pillars of Mexican humanism," saying no government in history has recognized their rights like the Fourth Transformation.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Puts Foreign Capital Under a National-Security Lens</u>

Sheinbaum's reform to the Foreign Investment Law will seat the heads of Public Security, Defense and the Navy on the commission that vets foreign takeovers in energy, AI, semiconductors and telecom. Morena rejects the framing that it's a favor to Washington: the bill "does not seek to benefit the United States or any particular nation" — just clear rules for the sectors that touch national security.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's elected judges file an austere first budget</u>

Mexico's first popularly elected judiciary filed its 2027 budget, and it's lean: 72.26 billion pesos, flat in real terms, with no salary increases and no private medical insurance for judges, El Economista reports. A year ago ex-Chief Justice Norma Piña demanded 17% more; this request comes in 13.7 billion pesos smaller — the judicial reform, showing up in the numbers.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US citizen arrested in Sonora for arming the Sinaloa Cartel</u>

In San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora, Mexican federal forces detained Yanet 'N,' a US citizen accused of working as an arms-trafficking logistics operator for a Sinaloa Cartel faction, seizing over 5,400 cartridges. A reminder of which way the weapons actually flow: roughly 80% of the guns fueling the cartels come from the United States.

✊🏾🇲🇽 <u>Mexico City hands Angela Davis the keys to the city</u>

At UNAM's FILUNI book fair, 82-year-old abolitionist Angela Davis presented 'Abolición, feminismo, ¡Ahora!' and told Mexico there is 'no place for despair,' calling for a feminism that is 'anticolonial, anticapitalist and antiracist.' Mayor Clara Brugada named her a distinguished visitor. Freedom, Davis said, 'is a constant struggle.'
banner: ANGELA DAVIS GETS KEYS TO CDMX

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Chiapas cuts daily homicides 64%</u>

Chiapas slashed its daily homicide average 64% — from 2.5 killings a day in December 2024 to 0.9 this August, its lowest level since 2015; vehicle theft fell 68%. 'It went from 2.4 to 0.9,' said SESNSP executive secretary Marcela Figueroa. Results from a Mexican security strategy under Governor Eduardo Ramírez — no foreign troops required.
